title: Rectangular base
spec: Create a new coordinate system by setting the Euler angles to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees. Translate this coordinate system using the vector [0.375, 0.0, 0.0]. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch of a rectangular face. Start by drawing the first line from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.0331, 0.0). Continue with the second line from (0.0331, 0.0) to (0.0331, 0.0038), then the third line from (0.0331, 0.0038) to (0.0, 0.0038), and finally the fourth line from (0.0, 0.0038) back to the origin. Apply a scale factor of 0.0331 to the entire sketch. Rotate the scaled sketch using the same Euler angles and translate it using the vector [0.375, 0.0, 0.0]. Extrude the transformed sketch 0.375 units along the normal direction, ensuring no extrusion occurs in the opposite direction. Finally, create a new solid body from the extruded sketch. The dimensions of the rectangular base are length 0.0331 units, width 0.0038 units, and height 0.375 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0331, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0331, 0.0038) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0038) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.375)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90) \
     .translate((0.375, 0.0, 0.0))

# Final model
r  # This will represent the final model
